title: Integrating Physics and Data-Driven Approaches: An Explainable and Uncertainty-Aware Hybrid Model for Wind Turbine Power Prediction
research_question: Can coupling kinematic wake physics with gradient-boosted trees improve operational wind farm yield forecasts under complex wake turbulence?
dataset: Commercial European multi-farm SCADA (>2 years, 10-min resolution across 3 complexes)
method: Hybrid 2-stream pipeline: Bastankhah-Porté-Agel analytical wake deficit coupled with XGBoost/LightGBM residual learners
main_claim: Hybridizing kinematic aerodynamic physics with tree-based residual estimators reduces farm-level power prediction error compared to pure data-driven models.
main_evidence: Reported 7.8% NMAE reduction and 9.4% NRMSE reduction across multi-turbine clusters under wake-affected wind directions.
negative_results: Explicitly reports that under free-stream inflow sectors (unwaked conditions), the physical model adds computational overhead without improving accuracy, matching unconstrained baselines.
ablation_design: Four-way ablation: Pure physics (analytical wake) vs Pure ML (unconstrained GBDT) vs Sequential Hybrid vs End-to-End Joint.
economic_evaluation: Evaluates forward delivery schedules and operational dispatch deviations, but without dynamic electricity balancing prices.
writing_style: Applied Energy empirical standard: active voice, problem-driven introduction, clear separation of site topography from model dynamics.
introduction_structure: P1: Grid decarbonization & wind variability; P2: Pure physics wake limitations; P3: Pure ML black-box overfitting; P4: Hybrid gap & proposed pipeline; P5: 3-point contribution.
results_structure: Question-led: Overall accuracy -> Directional sector breakdown -> Wake deficit resolution -> Inflow turbulence sensitivity.
discussion_structure: Mechanistic breakdown explaining why wake physics aids gradient search in turbulent waked regimes but is neutral in laminar flow.
limitations_structure: Dedicated subsection: highlights dependency on reliable upstream nacelle anemometry and yaw misalignment angles.
abstract_structure: Context (2 sentences) -> Problem & Gap (2 sentences) -> Proposed Hybrid Model (2 sentences) -> Key quantitative metrics (2 sentences) -> Practical implication (1 sentence).
usefulness_to_current_paper: Exemplar for Applied Energy narrative rhythm; demonstrates honest reporting of neutral physical regimes under free-stream conditions.

title: UniWind: Toward Unified Day-Ahead Wind Power Forecasting via Physics-Informed State Routing
research_question: Can dynamic routing between operational turbine states guided by physical power curve regimes improve multi-step day-ahead forecasting?
dataset: Three diverse Chinese commercial wind farms (flat, hilly, complex mountainous)
method: Physics-informed state router partitioning operational regimes (cut-in, rated, cut-out) into mixture-of-experts subnetworks
main_claim: State-dependent routing informed by empirical power curve inflection points improves ramp-event forecasting and day-ahead stability.
main_evidence: Outperforms Informer and PatchTST with 11.2% MAE improvement on 24-hour lookahead horizons.
negative_results: None reported in preprint; all reported metrics show uniform gains across all test sites.
ablation_design: Module-level ablation: Router excised (conflating gating parameters with physical boundaries). Audited in our corpus as S27.
economic_evaluation: Mentions day-ahead scheduling value qualitatively, but evaluates only symmetric MAE/RMSE without market settlement models.
writing_style: Dense architectural narrative; heavy emphasis on deep neural routing mechanisms.
introduction_structure: P1: Renewable energy integration; P2: Deep learning for time-series; P3: Neglect of aerodynamic regime transitions; P4: UniWind framework; P5: Itemized contributions.
results_structure: Benchmark comparison table -> Multi-horizon line plots -> Ramp event case studies -> Module ablation bar charts.

usefulness_to_current_paper: Key audited paper (S27); provides prime example of module-level ablation confounding to critique and benchmark against.

title: Day-ahead and real-time balancing dispatch mechanism under high renewable penetration
research_question: How do forecast uncertainty distributions propagate into reserve sizing and dispatch costs in two-stage market clearing?

title: Physics-informed reinforcement learning for power forecasting under extreme meteorological events
research_question: Can embedding turbine aerodynamic cutoff boundaries into reinforcement learning rewards prevent catastrophic forecast failure during typhoons?
dataset: Offshore wind farm telemetry in Guangdong, China during Typhoon Mangkhut and Typhoon Kompasu
method: Actor-critic RL embedding aerodynamic cut-out threshold penalty into reward function L_total = L_reward + lambda * L_aero
main_claim: Penalizing predictions violating aerodynamic cut-out envelopes prevents deep models from predicting full generation during storm shutdowns.
main_evidence: Eliminates high-power prediction spikes during turbine high-wind cut-out events; reduces peak event error by 34.2%.
negative_results: Notes that during normal operating conditions (wind speeds 6-15 m/s), the physical reward penalty has zero impact on error.
ablation_design: Ablation of physical reward penalty (lambda=0 vs lambda>0) and agent architecture.
economic_evaluation: Evaluates avoided extreme reserve imbalance penalties during storm events.
writing_style: Applied Energy case-study driven empirical narrative; high visual quality of storm tracking and cut-out profiles.
introduction_structure: P1: Extreme weather risks to grids; P2: Cut-out event forecasting failures; P3: Physics-informed RL gap; P4: Proposed framework; P5: Contributions.

title: The importance of atmospheric stability and turbulence in wind power curve modeling

writing_style: High-frequency financial econometrics applied to power markets; order book depth analysis, tick-level P&L curves.
introduction_structure: P1: Growth of continuous intraday markets; P2: Renewable forecast revisions; P3: Econometric literature; P4: Paper layout.
results_structure: Order book liquidity dynamics -> Forecast update value -> Execution backtest -> Slippage and transaction cost impact.
discussion_structure: Detailed discussion of the gap between theoretical market revenue on paper and realized execution cashflow in live trading.
limitations_structure: Focuses on the German EPEX market; results depend on specific market liquidity conditions.
abstract_structure: Intraday market expansion -> Forecast update trading potential -> High-frequency empirical study -> Surprising slippage results -> Trading conclusions.
usefulness_to_current_paper: Grounds our cautionary discussion on how market liquidity and transaction reality complicate simplistic paper cashflow models.

title: Leakage and the reproducibility crisis in machine-learning-based science
research_question: How widespread is data leakage in scientific machine learning, and how does it systematically inflate reported performance across disciplines?
dataset: Systematic audit of 329 machine learning papers across 17 distinct scientific disciplines
method: Multi-dimensional scoping review taxonomy classifying train-test leakage, feature leakage, and temporal distribution confounding
main_claim: Data leakage is a pervasive reproducibility threat in scientific AI, found in dozens of subfields and causing severe performance collapses upon correction.
main_evidence: Quantifies leakage prevalence across disciplines; re-implementation of affected models showed performance dropping to random chance.
negative_results: Exposes high-profile claims of breakthrough predictive accuracy as pure artifacts of circular preprocessing or temporal contamination.
ablation_design: Taxonomic audit matrix across 17 fields paired with forensic code-level re-implementation case studies.
economic_evaluation: Wasted scientific research funding and clinical/engineering deployment risks.
writing_style: Pinnacle of modern metascience; crystal-clear definitions, forensic case studies, dispassionate yet devastating critique.
introduction_structure: P1: ML boom across sciences; P2: The reproducibility crisis; P3: Taxonomy of data leakage failure modes; P4: Scope and roadmap.
results_structure: Prevalence across 17 disciplines -> Case studies of corrected performance -> Failure mode taxonomy -> Debugging protocols.
discussion_structure: Diagnoses academic incentive structures that reward unverified breakthrough claims while punishing rigorous negative results.
limitations_structure: Acknowledges that full detection of subtle leakage vectors is impossible without open, executable source code.
abstract_structure: Scientific ML growth -> Reproducibility failures -> 329-paper cross-disciplinary audit -> Severe leakage findings -> Remediation framework.
usefulness_to_current_paper: Primary methodological benchmark (TrackB_01) for our scoping audit (N=46), lifecycle taxonomy (D1-D5), and information budget analysis.

title: REFORMS: Consensus checklist for machine learning–based science
research_question: What reporting standards are required to ensure transparency, reproducibility, and rigorous evaluation in machine learning-based scientific claims?
dataset: Delphi consensus across 19 international experts spanning computer science, medicine, statistics, and physical sciences
method: Structured consensus methodology establishing a 32-item reporting checklist across five research lifecycle stages
main_claim: Scientific integrity in ML requires explicit disclosure across study goals, data hygiene, model architecture, baseline parity, and negative controls.
main_evidence: Extensive empirical literature audit showing that over 80% of published scientific ML papers omit critical checklist items.
negative_results: Documents that the majority of published 'breakthroughs' lack baseline parity, multiple random seeds, or negative controls.
ablation_design: Consensus checklist structure mapping lifecycle checkpoints: Goals -> Data -> Modeling -> Evaluation -> Transparency.
economic_evaluation: Scientific accountability and translational safety.
writing_style: Authoritative Science policy consensus style; concise, prescriptive, definitive, universally applicable.
introduction_structure: P1: Opportunities and pitfalls of AI in science; P2: Evidence of methodological failures; P3: The REFORMS initiative; P4: Checklist structure.
results_structure: The 32-item checklist presentation -> Module-by-module implementation guidance -> Peer review adoption guidelines.
discussion_structure: Emphasizes that checklists guide transparency but cannot substitute for domain-specific rigorous experimental designs.
limitations_structure: Checklist compliance cannot verify code execution fidelity without automated computational auditing.
abstract_structure: ML in science promise -> Pervasive reporting failures -> Expert consensus process -> The REFORMS 32-item standard -> Call for journal adoption.
usefulness_to_current_paper: Direct inspiration for Table 5 (our REFORMS-PCWPF five-gate reporting checklist, adapting C1-C5 to energy forecasting).

title: Troubling trends in machine learning scholarship
research_question: What systematic methodological, rhetorical, and empirical flaws undermine contemporary machine learning scholarship?
dataset: Qualitative literature survey across recent proceedings of NeurIPS, ICML, and ICLR
method: Epistemological critique identifying four diagnostic patterns: speculation vs explanation, failure to identify gains, mathiness, and misuse of language
main_claim: Machine learning literature frequently substitutes intuition for explanation, uses decorative math, and conflates correlation with causality.
main_evidence: Compelling case studies demonstrating how ablations fail to isolate empirical gains and how speculative narratives pass peer review.
negative_results: Exposes multiple published 'theories' that have zero bearing on the empirical success of the underlying algorithms.
ablation_design: Critique of uncalibrated ablation designs and failure to run proper control experiments.
economic_evaluation: Distortion of scientific priorities and misdirection of graduate research efforts.
writing_style: Witty, sharp, intellectually devastating, highly readable; sets the gold standard for constructive academic criticism.
introduction_structure: P1: The rapid expansion of ML; P2: Peer review strain; P3: The four diagnostic patterns introduced.
results_structure: Pattern 1: Speculation vs Explanation -> Pattern 2: Failure to Identify Gains -> Pattern 3: Mathiness -> Pattern 4: Misuse of Language.
discussion_structure: Actionable recommendations for authors, reviewers, and conference program chairs to raise scientific standards.
limitations_structure: Qualitative perspective paper without statistical cohort extraction.
abstract_structure: ML scholarship growth -> Pervasive bad habits -> Four diagnostic trends defined -> Constructive recommendations for the AI community.
usefulness_to_current_paper: Direct conceptual foundation for our Introduction and Discussion; cited in Section 1 to justify our critique of 'decorative math' and unisolated gains.

title: Improving reproducibility in machine learning research
research_question: How can institutional conference programs and submission checklists increase code sharing, data transparency, and experimental rigor?
dataset: Over 9,000 conference submissions to NeurIPS 2019 and 2020
method: Multi-year observational cohort study tracking the deployment of the NeurIPS Reproducibility Checklist and code submission mandates
main_claim: Mandatory checklists significantly increase code and data availability, but self-reported compliance does not guarantee execution fidelity.
main_evidence: Code submission rates rose from <50% to >75% following checklist introduction; error bar reporting doubled across submissions.
negative_results: Reveals that over 30% of submitted code repositories failed to execute out-of-the-box due to missing dependencies or data links.
ablation_design: Pre- vs post-policy intervention cohort comparison across compliance dimensions.
economic_evaluation: Institutional overhead of reproducibility verification in major scientific venues.
writing_style: Data-grounded institutional policy evaluation; precise registry counts, percentages, and author survey responses.
introduction_structure: P1: The reproducibility crisis in AI; P2: The NeurIPS initiative; P3: Program components; P4: Structure of report.
results_structure: Checklist compliance trends -> Code repository availability -> Reproducibility challenge findings -> Author feedback analysis.
discussion_structure: Distinguishes between superficial compliance (checking a box) and genuine scientific reproducibility (independent execution).
limitations_structure: Observational study without randomized control groups across conference submissions.
abstract_structure: Reproducibility challenge -> NeurIPS policy interventions -> Empirical evaluation across 9,000 papers -> Impact and remaining gaps.
usefulness_to_current_paper: Grounds our multi-seed reporting standards (5 seeds, means, standard deviations, paired bootstrap intervals) and code availability critique.

title: Machine learning for science: Methodological failures and recommendations
research_question: What recurring methodological mistakes lead ML models to appear successful in benchmarks but fail upon real scientific deployment?
dataset: Comprehensive cross-disciplinary review across biology, medical imaging, climate science, and materials
method: Diagnostic failure-mode taxonomy with concrete case studies illustrating distribution shift, metric gaming, and circular evaluation
main_claim: Benchmark success in scientific ML is frequently an illusion caused by deflated baselines, metric misalignment, and subtle distribution shifts.
main_evidence: Exposes high-profile medical and environmental AI papers whose claimed superior accuracy vanished upon testing on external hospital/sensor cohorts.
negative_results: Shows that simple linear baselines often match deep models when evaluated under proper external out-of-distribution protocols.
ablation_design: Analysis of common evaluation pitfalls: Trap 1 (Metric gaming), Trap 2 (Baseline deflation), Trap 3 (Distribution shift), Trap 4 (Circular validation).
economic_evaluation: Safety hazards and clinical/engineering failures of unverified scientific ML models.
writing_style: Pragmatic, expert, accessible; combines rigorous methodological insight with practical checklists for reviewers.
introduction_structure: P1: AI adoption in science; P2: The benchmark vs deployment paradox; P3: Purpose of guide; P4: Organization.
results_structure: Trap 1: Metric gaming -> Trap 2: Baseline deflation -> Trap 3: Distribution shifts -> Trap 4: Circular validation -> Reviewer checklist.
discussion_structure: Explains why machine learning benchmarks optimize for proxy targets that diverge from genuine scientific and operational goals.
limitations_structure: Recognizes that obtaining truly independent out-of-distribution test sets is difficult in observational science.
abstract_structure: AI in science boom -> The benchmark trap -> Four core methodological failures -> Real-world consequences -> Guidelines for reviewers and authors.
usefulness_to_current_paper: Direct methodological guidance for our critique of metric gaming, uncalibrated baselines, and our five-gate reporting checklist.

title: Closing the AI accountability gap: The role of internal and external algorithmic audits
journal: ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency (FAccT)
research_question: How can structured multi-stage auditing protocols hold algorithm developers accountable throughout the model development lifecycle?
dataset: Case studies of internal and external algorithmic audits across corporate, public sector, and scientific systems
method: Formulation of the Algorithmic Audit Lifecycle (SMAATR) separating development into Scoping, Mapping, Artifact Collection, Testing, and Reporting
main_claim: Accountability requires end-to-end lifecycle auditing from initial design choices to post-deployment telemetry, not merely post-hoc explainability.
main_evidence: Demonstrated that structured lifecycle auditing caught critical bias, data leakage, and software failures that black-box testing missed.
negative_results: Shows that post-hoc explainability tools (SHAP, LIME) frequently fail to detect severe training-loss implementation bugs.
ablation_design: Phase-by-phase lifecycle audit mapping requirements against concrete engineering artifacts.
economic_evaluation: Institutional compliance costs and liability mitigation in safety-critical automated systems.
writing_style: Professional auditing and governance metrology; clear lifecycle stages, auditable verification ledgers.
introduction_structure: P1: Deployed algorithmic harms; P2: Limitations of post-hoc transparency; P3: Lifecycle auditing proposal; P4: Paper structure.
results_structure: The SMAATR audit framework -> Lifecycle phase definitions -> Concrete audit artifacts -> Case study applications.
discussion_structure: Argues that engineering accountability requires auditable traces of software fidelity, parameter provenance, and testing boundaries.
limitations_structure: Trade-offs between proprietary confidentiality and public auditability in commercial deployments.
abstract_structure: Algorithmic accountability gap -> Post-hoc testing limitations -> Proposed lifecycle audit framework -> Real-world case studies -> Policy impact.
usefulness_to_current_paper: Direct theoretical foundation for our Five-Dimensional Constraint Lifecycle Taxonomy (D1-D5) in Section 4.1.

title: Deep reinforcement learning that matters
research_question: How do random seed selection, hyperparameter tuning, and code implementation differences confound empirical performance claims in deep RL?
dataset: OpenAI Gym benchmarks (MuJoCo, Atari) across 10+ random seeds and 5 distinct public codebases
method: Capacity-matched ablation holding algorithm structure constant while varying exclusively random seeds, code implementations, and reward scaling
main_claim: Reported performance differences between algorithms are frequently smaller than the variance across random seeds or code implementation bugs.
main_evidence: Demonstrates that identical algorithms implemented across different popular GitHub repositories produce non-overlapping performance distributions.
negative_results: Proves that cherry-picking top-performing random seeds can falsely make an inferior algorithm appear state-of-the-art.
ablation_design: Systematic factor isolation: Seed variance vs Codebase discrepancy vs Hyperparameter sensitivity vs Significance test validity.
economic_evaluation: Compute waste and misleading scientific trajectories in autonomous decision-making research.
writing_style: Pioneering forensic empirical audit style; uncompromising, rigorous, reproducible, heavy reliance on multi-seed confidence intervals.
introduction_structure: P1: Deep RL breakthrough claims; P2: The reproducibility challenge; P3: Experimental stress-testing methodology; P4: Roadmap.
results_structure: Random seed variance -> Codebase implementation divergence -> Hyperparameter tuning impacts -> Statistical significance guidelines.
discussion_structure: Exposes how minor implementation details (e.g., epsilon clamping, activation order) dominate algorithmic innovations.
limitations_structure: Focuses on continuous control and Atari benchmarks; results may differ in other domains.
abstract_structure: RL breakthroughs -> Reproducibility doubts -> Forensic empirical stress-tests -> Alarming seed and codebase divergences -> Reporting recommendations.
usefulness_to_current_paper: The gold-standard template for our software AST audit and our multi-seed empirical contrast between Reverse-JS and Standard-JS.

title: DOME: Recommendations for supervised machine learning validation in biology
research_question: What minimal reporting guidelines are required to ensure that supervised machine learning models in biological science are validated and reproducible?
dataset: Expert consensus across computational biology and biomedical machine learning communities
method: Four-pillar reporting framework: Data, Optimization, Model, and Evaluation (DOME)
main_claim: Scientific validity requires complete reporting across data provenance, split isolation, optimization stopping criteria, and out-of-distribution evaluation.
main_evidence: Systematic audit of published computational biology tools showing rampant data leakage and missing evaluation details.
negative_results: Documents numerous tools that fail completely when evaluated on data from different laboratories due to batch-effect leakage.
ablation_design: Structured reporting matrix mapping required disclosure items across the four DOME pillars.
economic_evaluation: Biomedical research translation safety and experimental resource waste.
writing_style: High-authority Nature Methods guideline style; crisp recommendations, structured tables, visual summary badges.
introduction_structure: P1: ML revolution in life sciences; P2: Validation deficits; P3: The DOME initiative; P4: Structure of recommendations.
results_structure: Data recommendations -> Optimization recommendations -> Model recommendations -> Evaluation recommendations.
discussion_structure: Discusses how community reporting standards improve peer review quality and model longevity.
limitations_structure: Focuses on supervised learning; unsupervised and generative models require specialized extensions.
abstract_structure: Supervised ML in biology -> Validation failures -> The DOME recommendations -> Community adoption roadmap.
usefulness_to_current_paper: Cited in our Discussion (Section 7.4) as the direct structural model for our five verification criteria (C1-C5).

title: State of the art: Reproducibility in artificial intelligence
research_question: To what degree do published empirical papers in premier AI conferences satisfy empirical, methodological, and computational reproducibility?
dataset: Systematic audit of 400 empirical papers published in AAAI and IJCAI (2013-2016)
method: Multi-category scoring framework evaluating disclosure of code, pseudo-code, data, hyperparameter ranges, and hardware specifications
main_claim: Fewer than 20% of published AI papers share executable source code, and fewer than 30% document complete experimental protocols.
main_evidence: Rigorous quantitative audit tables documenting that code availability remained stagnant despite exploding submission volumes.
negative_results: Shows that empirical claims of algorithm superiority cannot be replicated in over 70% of papers due to missing hyperparameter recipes.
ablation_design: Categorical compliance evaluation across 400 papers: Method reproducibility vs Data reproducibility vs Experiment reproducibility.
economic_evaluation: Wasted scientific labor attempting to reproduce undocumented baseline configurations.
writing_style: Classic AAAI empirical audit; structured percentage ledgers, statistical confidence intervals, uncompromising metrological tone.
introduction_structure: P1: Empirical science ideals in AI; P2: The reproducibility crisis; P3: The three-level reproducibility taxonomy; P4: Roadmap.
results_structure: Overall reproducibility rates -> Temporal trends -> Category-by-category breakdown -> Code availability deficit.
discussion_structure: Analyzes the structural reasons for poor reproducibility: lack of reviewer incentives, proprietary software, fear of scrutiny.
limitations_structure: Relies on published text and supplementary material; authors were not contacted directly.
abstract_structure: AI empirical nature -> Reproducibility audit of 400 papers -> Low code/data sharing findings -> Call for community reform.
usefulness_to_current_paper: Direct precedent for our literature audit in Section 5.1 and our reporting of the 95.7% open-code deficit.

title: Underspecification presents challenges for credibility in modern machine learning
research_question: Why do neural networks that achieve identical in-distribution test accuracy diverge catastrophically when deployed under real-world distribution shift?
dataset: Multi-domain benchmarks across medical imaging, natural language processing, computer vision, and epidemiology
method: Controlled stress-testing training multiple random seeds with identical architecture and loss, evaluating out-of-distribution divergence
main_claim: Standard empirical risk minimization is severely underspecified: distinct models with identical test accuracy encode radically different predictive shortcuts.
main_evidence: Shows that 10 models trained with different random seeds achieve identical in-distribution accuracy but exhibit 40-60% performance variance on stress-test shifts.
negative_results: Demonstrates that nominal in-distribution test performance provides near-zero indication of real-world operational reliability.
ablation_design: Multi-seed stress-testing across domain-specific distribution shifts holding in-distribution test accuracy strictly constant.
economic_evaluation: Deployment safety hazards in medical diagnosis, credit scoring, and autonomous vehicle navigation.
writing_style: Profound, rigorous, landmark JMLR style; clear mathematical formulation of hypothesis spaces, extensive empirical stress-tests.
introduction_structure: P1: ML benchmark success vs deployment failure; P2: Defining underspecification; P3: Multi-domain evidence preview; P4: Roadmap.
results_structure: Computer vision stress-tests -> Medical imaging divergence -> NLP shortcut learning -> Stress-testing guidelines.
discussion_structure: Explains why inductive biases and loss regularization can either constrain underspecification or introduce damaging rigid shortcuts.
limitations_structure: Designing comprehensive out-of-distribution stress-tests requires domain-specific operational expertise.
abstract_structure: ML credibility crisis -> Definition of underspecification -> Empirical demonstration across disciplines -> Implications for safety -> Solutions.
usefulness_to_current_paper: Provides the epistemological framework explaining why physical constraints can appear beneficial under nominal testing while failing under operational shifts.
